title: Self assembly, structure and properties of the decanuclear lanthanide ring complex, Dy10(OC2H4OCH3)30

synthesis.procedure: All syntheses were carried out in a glove box under dry oxygen-free argon using glassware dried at 150 °C and solvents dried by distillation from CaH2. Route (i): dysprosium chips (1.732 g, 10.66 mmol) were treated with ca 0.3 mg HgCl2 in 20 mL methoxyethanol:toluene (1:1 v/v) and heated to 70–80 °C. After 24–48 h the mixture was centrifuged to sediment olive-green finely divided DyH3−x; the pale yellow solution was evaporated in vacuum to leave moisture-sensitive crystalline or sticky Dy10(MOE)30 (yield ca 50%). Route (ii): potassium (0.625 g, 16.0 mmol) was dissolved in 20 mL MOEH+toluene (1:2 v/v) and DyCl3 (1.433 g, 5.328 mmol) was added. After 48 h stirring the mixture was centrifuged to separate KCl and the solution evaporated, leaving solid Dy10(MOE)30 (ca 90–95% yield). Crystallization was slow. UV–vis–NIR and IR spectra of the two products were identical.
synthesis.temperature: 70–80 °C (route i); ambient stirring (route ii, not specified beyond 48 h)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: glove box under dry oxygen-free argon; centrifugation and vacuum evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Route i: centrifuge off DyH3−x, evaporate pale yellow solution in vacuum to a moisture-sensitive crystalline or sticky solid. Route ii: centrifuge off KCl, evaporate solution; crystallization was slow.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χT ≈ 138 emu mol−1 K agrees with ten free Dy3+ ions (140 emu mol−1 K). χT decreases on cooling, attributed to crystal-field/anisotropy effects rather than exchange. Magnetization saturates at about 48 μB at 3 T and 2 K, indicating weak exchange within the Dy10 ring is masked by crystal-field effects.
